name: The Pantheon
description: Former Roman temple featuring the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome, crowned by an open central oculus.
history: Commissioned by Marcus Agrippa during the reign of Augustus and completely rebuilt by Emperor Hadrian c. 126 CE.
construction: Engineered with volcanic pozzolana concrete that gradually lightens in density toward the top using pumice aggregates.
architecture: Octastyle Corinthian portico opening into a rotunda of exact proportion: the interior height and diameter are equal at 43.3 meters.
significance: The best-preserved Roman monument in existence and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
currentStatus: Standing pristine in Piazza della Rotonda, Rome.
